try_hover_focus_and_accessible_states_sk.title: Try it yourself: Make links respond when a pointer reaches them
try_hover_focus_and_accessible_states_sk.prompt:
Now apply what you just learned in this task. ## CSS task

The links now share the portfolio's accent `color`, but they look exactly the same when a pointer moves over them. That makes the interaction feel flat. Use the stronger accent token for feedback: add `a:hover { color: var(--color-accent-strong); }`. Move the pointer across links in the preview; their `color` should deepen while the default state remains unchanged.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on. Produce the result for make links respond when a pointer reaches them so it reinforces Hover, Focus, and Accessible States.

try_hover_focus_and_accessible_states_sk.title: Try it yourself: Make keyboard focus easy to see
try_hover_focus_and_accessible_states_sk.prompt:
Now apply what you just learned in this task. ## CSS task

Pointer users can now see hover feedback, but keyboard users also need a clear signal as they tab through the page. Do not remove focus outlines. Add `a:focus-visible` with a `0.2rem solid #f59e0b` `outline` and `0.2rem` `outline-offset`. Then use the keyboard to move through the links: the focused link should be obvious without changing the layout around it.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on. Produce the result for make keyboard focus easy to see so it reinforces Hover, Focus, and Accessible States.

try_hover_focus_and_accessible_states_sk.title: Try it yourself: Keep the real contact button readable when it is active
try_hover_focus_and_accessible_states_sk.prompt:
Now apply what you just learned in this task. ## CSS task

The Contact page already has a real submit button, so its interaction states should feel as intentional as the links. Right now the button does not share the stronger accent feedback. Add a grouped `button:hover, button:focus-visible` rule with `background: var(--color-accent-strong);` and `color: #fff;`. Hover the button and tab to it in the preview: both states should use the stronger `background` while the label stays clearly readable.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on. Produce the result for keep the real contact button readable when it is active so it reinforces Hover, Focus, and Accessible States.

Pointer users can now see hover feedback, but keyboard users also need a clear signal as they tab through the page. Do not remove focus outlines. try-hover-focus-and-accessible-states-sk.title: Keep the real contact button readable when it is active
try-hover-focus-and-accessible-states-sk.prompt:
## CSS task

The Contact page already has a real submit button, so its interaction states should feel as intentional as the links. Right now the button does not share the stronger accent feedback. Add a grouped `button:hover, button:focus-visible` rule with `background: var(--color-accent-strong);` and `color: #fff;`. Hover the button and tab to it in the preview: both states should use the stronger `background` while the label stays clearly readable.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
try-hover-focus-and-accessible-states-sk.hint: Target the existing `button` element directly; group hover and focus-visible so they share the same readable state.

help.concept: Accessible component states should remain visually distinct and keep enough foreground/`background` contrast.
help.hint_1: Use the existing button—there is no need to invent a `.button-link` class.
help.hint_2: Group the two pseudo-class selectors with a comma and keep the text white on the stronger accent `background`.
